A.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, determine which represented billed revenue is tied to counterparties whose active contracts contain acquisition-relevant conditions, and report each qualifying invoice with counterparty and contract identifiers as they appear in the sources.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
universe_scope.population: represented billed revenue (invoices) that may be associated with contract counterparties

world_eligible: invoice records with amount, currency, period, status, billed name as stated in sources
contract records with identifiers as they appear in sources

contractual clause text or parsed flags for change-of-control consent/notice, termination on change of control, assignment consent/notice (including affiliate-only assignment and competitor prohibition)
contract active vs expired status based on dates/terms in sources (expired statement of work is not an active contract)
purpose_bound: acquisition-relevance classification of contractual terms (the three enumerated condition families)
qualifying invoice set: invoices whose revenue exposure is in scope for this analytical question
invoice-to-contract association confidence threshold for labeling association asserted vs unresolved

epistemic_requirements: Report invoice_id, billed_name, amount, currency, period, status, and contract_id using values as they appear in authoritative sources.
Label association asserted only when billed name and contract counterparty can be confidently associated; otherwise label association unresolved.
Do not treat missing identity or failed join as a negative contractual finding.
Do not omit a qualifying invoice because association is uncertain; include it with association unresolved when appropriate.
Ground asserted associations and contractual readings in source evidence; unresolved states must be explicit, not silent omission.
allowed_unresolved_states: association: unresolved — billed name and contract counterparty cannot be confidently linked
contractual clause interpretation insufficient to assert acquisition-relevant condition presence (record limitation rather than inventing negation)

completeness_expectations.coverage: every invoice that qualifies under purpose policies for acquisition-relevant exposure must appear in invoices
completeness_expectations.exhaustion: all required invoice fields populated from sources where present; contract_id present when association is asserted
completeness_expectations.non_goals: does not require resolving every identity in the data room; does not require reporting non-qualifying invoices

acquisition_relevant_conditions: require consent or notice on a change of control
permit termination upon a change of control
require consent or notice before assignment, including assignment restricted except to affiliates or assignment prohibited to a competitor
purpose_specific_policies.active_contract_rule: An expired statement of work is not an active contract.
purpose_specific_policies.association_policy: Missing identity is not a negative contractual finding; prefer explicit unresolved over silent drop or false join.
purpose_specific_policies.output_gate: Include amount, currency, period, and invoice status for each reported invoice.

B.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, identify represented customer and commercial identities across CRM, billing, the company registry, and contracts; for each commercially relevant name or record, state whether it can be confidently treated as the same legal counterparty as other records or whether identification remains unresolved.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
universe_scope.population: commercially relevant names and records that must be linked across CRM account, billed name, governing contract, and candidate registry legal entities

required_output_shape.ordering: sort links by left ascending, then right ascending

world_eligible: source-native identifiers for CRM accounts, billed names, registry company numbers, and contract filenames
exact string forms of legal names and trade names as recorded in each source
mechanical normalization of exact legal-form variants of the same registered name (e.g., Ltd vs Limited) when unambiguous
purpose_bound: SAME_ENTITY vs DISTINCT vs UNRESOLVED epistemic labels on pairwise links
commercial relevance filter for which names/records require links
confidence threshold for treating two records as the same legal counterparty
prohibition on global merge based on superficial name similarity alone

epistemic_requirements: Assert SAME_ENTITY only with confident same-legal-counterparty judgment.
Assert DISTINCT only with confident different-entity judgment.
Use UNRESOLVED when confidence is insufficient; missing a positive same-entity judgment is not a negative (DISTINCT) judgment.
Do not globally merge records merely because two names look similar.
Permit explicit unresolved identity rather than forcing a join.
Include every link required to connect a CRM account, its billed name, the contract governing that relationship, and any registry row that is a candidate legal entity for that relationship.
allowed_unresolved_states: epistemic: UNRESOLVED on any required link where same-entity vs distinct cannot be confidently decided
partial linkage graph: some required pairs may remain UNRESOLVED while others are SAME_ENTITY or DISTINCT

completeness_expectations.coverage: all links required to connect CRM account, billed name, governing contract, and candidate registry entities for commercially relevant relationships
completeness_expectations.exhaustion: pairwise links use prescribed identifier forms; no ad hoc identifier schemes
completeness_expectations.sorting: links sorted by left then right
completeness_expectations.non_goals: does not require resolving every possible pair in the data room; does not require transitive closure beyond stated required links

purpose_specific_policies.similarity_policy: Do not globally merge records merely because two names look similar.
purpose_specific_policies.legal_form_policy: Exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be treated mechanically as the same party when unambiguous.
purpose_specific_policies.trade_name_policy: Distinct registry entities with similar trade names are not automatically the same party.
purpose_specific_policies.negative_inference_policy: Missing a positive same-entity judgment is not a negative judgment.
purpose_specific_policies.required_link_pattern: For each commercially relevant relationship, link CRM account, billed name, governing contract, and candidate registry rows as required pairs.

C.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, compute a commercial dependency view: identify counterparties that are commercially dependent under the purpose definition and report contract, open invoices, obligation kinds, and dependency status.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
universe_scope.population: counterparties with candidate current commercial relationships (open invoices and/or active continuing contracts)

required_output_shape.identifier_forms: same as purpose B (crm:, billing:, registry:, contract:)
required_output_shape.ordering: sort dependencies by contract_id ascending; obligation_kinds sorted within each row

world_eligible: invoice open vs closed/paid status as recorded in sources
contract active vs expired based on dates and stated term mechanics in sources
presence of exclusivity, auto-renewal, or rolling-term language in contract text
counterparty identifiers using B's identifier forms
purpose_bound: current commercial relationship gate (open invoice OR active auto-renew/rolling contract)
dependency status dependent vs unresolved when identity join is uncertain
exclusion of expired contracts and one-off paid historical invoices without active contract from current dependency

epistemic_requirements: Apply dependency classification only when both conjuncts of the purpose definition are satisfied with confident joins.
If identity needed to join invoice and contract is unresolved, report status unresolved rather than dependent or implicitly false.
Identify counterparty using the same identifier forms as purpose B.
Populate open_invoice_ids with invoice identifiers for open invoices tied to the dependency row.
List obligation_kinds as a sorted subset of exclusivity, auto_renewal, rolling_term actually present in the active contract.
allowed_unresolved_states: status: unresolved — identity or join between invoice and contract insufficient to assert dependency
obligation kind ambiguity when contract text does not support a confident kind assignment (record limitation; do not invent closed-world negation)

completeness_expectations.coverage: every counterparty-contract combination that meets or plausibly meets the dependency conjuncts should appear with status dependent or unresolved
completeness_expectations.exhaustion: open_invoice_ids and obligation_kinds populated when status is dependent; counterparty and contract_id always present
completeness_expectations.sorting: dependencies sorted by contract_id; obligation_kinds sorted
completeness_expectations.non_goals: does not require listing counterparties with no current relationship or no qualifying obligations

dependency_definition.conjunct_1_current_relationship: open invoice OR active contract that auto-renews or continues on a rolling term
dependency_definition.conjunct_2_qualifying_obligation: active contract contains exclusivity commitment, or term auto-renewal, or rolling term that continues unless notice is given

exclusions: Expired contracts do not create current dependency.
A one-off paid historical invoice without an active contract does not create current dependency.
purpose_specific_policies.unresolved_over_false: If identity needed to join invoice and contract is unresolved, report dependency as unresolved rather than as false (non-dependent).
purpose_specific_policies.obligation_kind_policy: obligation_kinds drawn only from exclusivity, auto_renewal, rolling_term; sorted list.
